title: The Thorn of Ashvale
premise: Kestrel Galloway, a beast-speaker concealing his forbidden gift beneath a clerk's quiet life, discovers his own name and tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies held by the Ashvale Guild of Impossible Things. The prophecy foretells that the 'Thorn' — the last living vessel of an ancient war-god's power — will be revealed on this night, and every faction in the city will kill to claim or destroy it. As Kestrel unravels the guild's ledgers, he learns the Thorn is not a person but a choice: the power passes to whoever knowingly accepts it, and accepting it means becoming the tyrant the old war was fought to prevent. Hunted by the guild's enforcers, courted by rebels, and betrayed by the mentor who wrote the prophecy to trap him, Kestrel must decide whether truth or loyalty will save Ashvale. In the end he speaks the secret aloud to the city, shattering the prophecy's grip, and lets the power die with him — only to wake, changed but free, as something no book ever predicted.
about_author: Kestrel Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rare manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside other people's stories, and live near the coast with an opinionated dog.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night of routine inventory at the Ashvale Guild: caged songs, bottled storms, a debt owed by a duke. Kestrel quietly converses with the guild's rats, hiding his beast-speech even from himself. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man fluent in everything except honesty.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than the Author
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. While rebinding a damaged volume, he finds a prophecy book dated a century past — and reads his own name beside tonight's date. He tells himself it's coincidence. Emotional beat: cold dread masquerading as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Rats Have Seen
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The guild's rats warn him strangers searched the archives by night. His mentor, Archivist Sorrel Vane, deflects his questions with warmth that feels rehearsed. Emotional beat: first crack in trust; loyalty begins to feel like a leash.

chapters.title: A Visitor from the Old War
chapters.summary: Maren Oduya's POV. A rebel courier infiltrates the guild hunting the prophecy book, believing it can stop the coming war. She nearly catches Kestrel mid-beast-speech. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Date Arrives
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On the prophesied night, the guild seals its doors for a private auction. Every faction in Ashvale attends under false names. Kestrel realizes he isn't a witness to the prophecy — he's the lot being sold. Emotional beat: vertigo of a life revealed as someone else's design.

chapters.title: Sold to the Highest Bidder
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Sorrel auctions knowledge of the Thorn's identity, revealing fragments that point unmistakably to Kestrel. Bidders include a guild enforcer, a palace spymaster, and Maren disguised. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a mentor's face.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Caged Songs
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel flees through the vaults, releasing beasts and impossible things as cover. The freed creatures follow him, speaking his name in a hundred voices. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear — his gift exposed, his old life burned.

chapters.title: The Rebel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren shelters Kestrel in the rebel Warrens and offers protection in exchange for the prophecy book's location. Kestrel lies about what he knows. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging, built on a fresh lie.

chapters.title: Reading the Thorn
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the Warrens' hidden library, Kestrel deciphers the full prophecy: the Thorn is a mantle of the war-god's power that transfers to whoever knowingly claims it. The prophecy was written to manufacture its own heir. Emotional beat: horror at realizing words can be weapons.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Corvus Hale's POV. Palace spymaster Corvus offers Kestrel amnesty and purpose: become the Thorn deliberately, controlled by the crown, and end the war before it starts. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Beasts Do Not Lie
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hiding in the menagerie district, Kestrel hears the city's animals repeating fragments of the prophecy — it has infected their speech too. He understands the words are rewriting reality itself. Emotional beat: grief for a world where language could still be trusted.

chapters.title: Maren's Truth
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses she was sent not to save Kestrel but to kill the Thorn if claiming it proved necessary. Kestrel forgives her — then admits his own lies. Emotional beat: two broken loyalties choosing fragile honesty.

chapters.title: The Guild Reclaims Its Property
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Enforcers storm the Warrens. Sorrel captures Kestrel, revealing she authored the prophecy under her true, much older name — she needs an heir because the Thorn is killing her. Emotional beat: pity entangled with fury.

chapters.title: Chains of Paper
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Imprisoned in the guild vaults, Kestrel is bound by contract-magic: his voice literally cannot speak the Thorn's secret aloud. Sorrel prepares the transfer ritual. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair — silenced by ink.

chapters.title: The Rats Remember Everything
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The freed beasts and guild rats gnaw through the contract-ledgers, unbinding Kestrel's voice. Maren and rebel sympathizers breach the vaults. Emotional beat: hope arriving small, toothy, and improbable.

chapters.title: What Sorrel Buried
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Confronted, Sorrel admits the original war began when the last Thorn refused to surrender the god's power — and that she has spent a century engineering a successor so she can finally rest. Emotional beat: a villain's tragedy laid bare.

chapters.title: The Ritual Begins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sorrel initiates the transfer anyway, forcing the choice: accept the Thorn willingly or let it pass to Corvus, who waits in the wings with the crown's blessing. Emotional beat: terror of a decision where every door leads somewhere terrible.

chapters.title: The Word That Breaks the Book
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax. Instead of accepting or refusing, Kestrel speaks the prophecy's full text aloud to the assembled factions — exposing the manipulation to all. Unspoken truths lose their power when witnessed; the book begins to burn from within. Emotional beat: liberation through radical honesty.

chapters.title: Ashvale Chooses
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. With the prophecy dying, the factions turn on each other — until the freed beasts flood the hall, mirroring back each speaker's true intentions. The crowd sees itself clearly. Emotional beat: collective reckoning; the war starves without its fuel of secrets.

chapters.title: The Price of Speaking
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The dying Thorn-power, needing a vessel, pours into Kestrel as the book burns. He carries it to the old battlefield and lets it dissolve into the ground rather than into anyone. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs him his gift — the beasts fall silent to him.

chapters.title: A Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Weeks later, Kestrel rebuilds the guild as an honest archive, with Maren as partner and Sorrel's records opened to the city. Deaf now to beasts, he learns human speech again — saying what he means. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Something No Book Predicted
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, final pages shifting outward. A stray dog speaks one word to him — proof some thread of the gift survived, changed and unbound by any prophecy. Kestrel laughs for the first time in the book. Emotional beat: open-ended wonder; identity chosen, not assigned.
